summary: Joshua T. Katz is a linguist who studied at the Dalton School, Yale University (~1989–1993), the University of Oxford (~1993–1995), and Harvard University (~1995–1998). He held a post at Princeton University from 1998 to 2022.
Joshua W. C. Cutler specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Wangyal (~1970–1983) and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center around 1983.

Josiah Royce (1855–1916) was a philosopher who studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1871–1875) and Johns Hopkins University (~1876–1878). He held positions at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and Harvard University (~1882–1916).

José Ignacio Cabezón works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Caltech, Sera Monastery, and UW–Madison (Ph.D. under Geshe Lhundub Sopa). He held posts at Iliff School of Theology, University of Denver, University of Hamburg, and UC Santa Barbara.
José van den Broeck is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Université catholique de Louvain under Étienne Lamotte, completing a doctoral thesis around 1977.
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London (~2007–2012) under the supervision of Kate Crosby.

Jowita Kramer works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning degrees at Hamburg (under Lambert Schmithausen) and Munich. She has held posts at UC Berkeley, Oxford, Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Joy Brennan specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago (~2007–2015), where her dissertation committee included Matthew T. Kapstein, Dan Arnold, and Paul Copp.
Juan Wu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Cardiff University (~2008–2012) under the supervision of Max Deeg.

Judit Törzsök works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at the University of Lille, CNRS, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Judith A. Berling specializes in religious studies and sinology. She studied at Carleton College (~1959–1963) and Columbia University (~1968–1976), and served as a professor at the Graduate Theological Union (~1987–2019).

Judith Simmer-Brown works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Western Washington University and under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, serving as chair of the Religious Studies Department at Naropa University in 1977.

Juhn Y. Ahn works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (~2001–2007) and became Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies at the University of Michigan around 2014.

Juhyung Rhi works in Buddhist studies and art history. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (~1984–1991) and was appointed Professor of Art History at Seoul National University in 1992.
Juichiro Tanabe works in religious studies and other fields. He was a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford (2000–2010) and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn until 2006.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire (1805–1895) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and Bourbon College. He held posts at the Collège de France (1838–1852) and Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques (~1839–1895).

Jules Bloch (1880–1953) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Lycée Charlemagne, École Pratique des Hautes Études, ENLOV, and University of Paris. He held posts at EPHE, ENLOV, Collège de France, University of Lyon, and University of Paris.

Jules Brooks Levinson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (~1982–1994) under Jeffrey Hopkins and served as Assistant Professor in the Department of Religion at Hamline University.

Jules Michelet (1798–1874) was a historian who studied at Lycée Charlemagne (1812–1816). He held posts at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour, École Normale Supérieure, the Archives nationales (1830–1852), and the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Jules Mohl (1800–1876) worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Sinological studies. Educated at the University of Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy and Abel-Rémusat, he held posts at Tübingen, the Société Asiatique, and the Collège de France.
